key_insight: Two-way coupling between superfluid vortices and normal-fluid turbulence causes quantized vortices in superfluid helium to organize into coherent bundles inside vortex tubes, reproducing a classical turbulence-like hierarchy across scales.
engineering_relevance: The result provides a mechanistic basis for predicting multiscale vortex organization, dissipation, and thermal stability in cryogenic two-fluid flow systems.
method: Fully coupled vortex filament model with Navier–Stokes equations
Track mutual friction, vortex bundling, and energy spectra across scales
evidence_signal: The abstract reports simulation evidence showing bundle formation, a time lag between superfluid kinetic energy and dissipation, and a Kolmogorov $k^{-5/3}$ spectrum.
watch_item: The bundling criterion and stability conclusions may depend on the simulated coupling regime and periodic forcing, so applicability to more general geometries should be checked.
paper_title: Two-Way Coupled Dynamics of Quantized Vortex Bundle Formation in Spatially Periodic Normal-Fluid Turbulence
